claims.text: The interplay between composition and microstructure governs the premelting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The interplay between composition and microstructure governs the melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Composition and microstructure influence defect formation in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Composition and microstructure influence the grain boundaries present in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Composition and microstructure influence the interfaces present in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Defects influence the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Grain boundaries influence the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Interfaces influence the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Interactions among defects, grain boundaries, and interfaces lead to premelting and melting behavior.
Nanoparticles with optimized composition and microstructure will have greater thermal stability than nanoparticles with random composition and microstructure.
Optimized composition and microstructure will reduce the premelting temperature relative to the random-composition and random-microstructure baseline.
Optimized composition and microstructure will reduce the melting temperature relative to the random-composition and random-microstructure baseline.
The hypothesis is expected to hold from 300 to 1000 K.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for nanoparticles containing three to ten principal elements.
The hypothesis is expected to hold across microstructures ranging from crystalline to amorphous.

contradictions.description: The outcome describes reduced premelting and melting temperatures as enhanced thermal stability. Lower transition temperatures ordinarily indicate reduced resistance to thermal transformation unless a different definition of thermal stability is supplied.
